extracted.intended_audience: state agency officials, regulated persons/businesses, administrative law judges, attorneys practicing Florida administrative law
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory procedural and substantive standards from the Florida Administrative Procedure Act covering licensing, investigations, exemptions, administrative law judges, rulemaking plans, hearings, ex parte communications, judicial review, and enforcement. Useful for agencies, regulated parties, and lawyers to comply with and evaluate administrative processes under Florida law.

rubrics_metrics.name: License renewal pendency tolling of expiration
rubrics_metrics.description: A license does not expire until the application for renewal has been finally acted upon by the agency or, in case the application is denied or the terms of the license are limited, until the last day for seeking review of the agency order or a later date fixed by order of the reviewing court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule provides tolling of expiration while renewal is pending and, where renewal is denied or limited, preserves rights until the end of the review period or later court order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requirement before license revocation or suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: No revocation, suspension, annulment, or withdrawal of any license is lawful unless, prior to the entry of a final order, the agency has served, by personal service or certified mail, an administrative complaint which affords reasonable notice to the licensee of facts or conduct which warrant the intended action and unless the licensee has been given an adequate opportunity to request a proceeding pursuant to ss. 120.569 and 120.57.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If personal service cannot be made and certified mail is returned undelivered, the agency must publish a short, plain notice once each week for 4 consecutive weeks in a newspaper published in the county of the licensee’s last known address (or in a paper of general circulation in that county if no county paper exists).

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency suspension procedure requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If the agency finds that immediate serious danger to the public health, safety, or welfare requires emergency suspension, restriction, or limitation of a license, the agency may take such action by any procedure that is fair under the circumstances if: (a) the procedure provides at least the same procedural protection as given by other statutes or constitutions; (b) the agency takes only that action necessary to protect the public interest under the emergency procedure; and (c) the agency states in writing at the time of, or prior to, its action the specific facts and reasons for finding an immediate danger and for concluding that the procedure used is fair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency’s findings of immediate danger, necessity, and procedural fairness are judicially reviewable. Summary suspension, restriction, or limitation may be ordered, but a suspension or revocation proceeding under ss. 120.569 and 120.57 must also be promptly instituted and acted upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on conditions of approval based on other agency statements
rubrics_metrics.description: No agency shall include as a condition of approval of any license any provision that is based upon a statement, policy, or guideline of another agency unless the statement, policy, or guideline is within the jurisdiction of the other agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The other agency must identify for the licensing agency the specific legal authority for each such statement, policy, or guideline. The licensing agency must provide the licensee an opportunity to challenge the condition as invalid. Any party to an administrative proceeding arising from the approval with conditions or denial may require the other agency to join as a party to determine the validity of the condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights in agency investigations — transcript and counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: Every person who responds to a request or demand by any agency or representative thereof for written data or an oral statement shall be entitled to a transcript or recording of his or her oral statement at no more than cost. Any person compelled to appear, or who appears voluntarily, before any presiding officer or agency in an investigation or in any agency proceeding has the right, at his or her own expense, to be accompanied, represented, and advised by counsel or by other qualified representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entitles respondents to a copy of their oral statement and to representation in investigations and proceedings; transcript cost is limited to no more than cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds and procedures for exemption from the APA by Administration Commission
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon application of any agency, the Administration Commission may exempt any process or proceeding governed by this act from one or more requirements of this act when: (a) the agency head certifies the requirement would conflict with federal law or rules; (b) to permit persons in the state to receive tax benefits or federal funds under federal law; or (c) conformity with the requirements would be so inconvenient or impractical as to defeat the purpose of the agency proceeding or the act and would not be in the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before granting an exemption the commission must establish alternative procedures consistent with the intent and purpose of the act; hold a public hearing with notice as provided in s. 120.525; issue an order granting or denying the exemption and specify any alternative procedures; transmit copies to specified entities and publish notice in the Florida Administrative Register. Exemptions terminate 90 days after adjournment sine die of the next regular legislative session (or upon legislative incorporation), may be renewed no more than once, and alternative procedures must be established prior to exempting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications and appointment of director and administrative law judges
rubrics_metrics.description: The Division of Administrative Hearings shall be headed by a director appointed by the Administration Commission and confirmed by the Senate; the director, who shall also serve as the chief administrative law judge, and any deputy chief administrative law judge must possess the same minimum qualifications as the administrative law judges employed by the division. Any person employed by the division as an administrative law judge must have been a member of The Florida Bar in good standing for the preceding 5 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies minimum bar membership requirement for ALJs and that the director and deputy chief must meet those same qualifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division independence and administrative support
rubrics_metrics.description: The Division of Administrative Hearings shall be a separate budget entity; the director shall be its agency head for all purposes. The Department of Management Services shall provide administrative support and service to the division to the extent requested by the director. The division shall not be subject to control, supervision, or direction by the Department of Management Services in any manner, including personnel, purchasing, transactions involving real or personal property, and budgetary matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes structural independence of the division and the limits of departmental control; administrative support is provided only as requested by the director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's appeal rights regarding division budget/personnel decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The director has the right to appeal actions by the Executive Office of the Governor that affect amendments to the division’s approved operating budget or any personnel actions pursuant to chapter 216 to the Administration Commission, which shall decide such issue by majority vote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriations committees may advise the Administration Commission; if the President of the Senate and Speaker object in writing, the appeal may be affirmed only by a two-thirds vote of commission members present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual reporting by the Division of Administrative Hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Not later than February 1 of each year, the division shall issue a written report to the Administrative Procedures Committee and the Administration Commission including at least: (a) summary of agencies’ utilization of ALJs, court reporters, and personnel in proceedings under this chapter; (b) recommendations for change or improvement in the APA or agency practices; (c) recommendations as to case types appropriate for summary hearing process described in s. 120.574; and (d) a report regarding each agency’s compliance with the filing requirement in s. 120.57(1)(m).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual reporting requirement sets out specific content the division must include, supporting oversight and potential reform recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reimbursement and contracting for ALJ services to specified entities
rubrics_metrics.description: The division shall be reimbursed for administrative law judge services and travel expenses by specified entities (water management districts, regional planning councils, school districts, community colleges, the Division of Florida Colleges, state universities, Board of Governors, State Board of Education, Florida School for the Deaf and Blind, Commission for Independent Education). These entities shall contract with the division to establish a contract rate based on a total-cost-recovery methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires contracting for services and travel/video teleconferencing expense reimbursement and bases contract rates on total-cost-recovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation and qualifications of ALJs for Department of Health matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The Division of Administrative Hearings shall designate at least two administrative law judges who shall specifically preside over actions involving the Department of Health or boards within the Department of Health. Each designated administrative law judge must be a member of The Florida Bar in good standing and must have legal, managerial, or clinical experience in issues related to health care or have attained board certification in health care law from The Florida Bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires specialized assignment and subject-matter-related experience or certification for health-related administrative adjudications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withholding school district funds to pay for ALJ services
rubrics_metrics.description: If a district school board fails to make a timely payment for services provided by an administrative law judge as provided annually in the General Appropriations Act, the Commissioner of Education shall withhold from any general revenue funds the district is eligible to receive an amount sufficient to pay for the administrative law judge’s services and transfer it to the Division of Administrative Hearings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates a statutory mechanism to secure payment for ALJ services provided to school districts by withholding and transferring state funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte communications prohibition and remedial measures
rubrics_metrics.description: In any proceeding under ss. 120.569 and 120.57, no ex parte communication relative to the merits, threat, or offer of reward shall be made to the agency head after the agency head has received a recommended order, or to the presiding officer, by: (a) an agency head or public employee engaged in prosecution or advocacy in connection with the matter; or (b) a party to the proceeding, the party’s authorized representative or counsel, or any person who would have a substantial interest in the proposed action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A presiding officer who receives an improper ex parte communication must place all written communications and written responses on the record, memorialize oral communications, advise all parties, and allow any party to request rebuttal within 10 days. The presiding officer may withdraw to eliminate the effect of the communication, and violators (or presiding officers who fail to place communications on the record) may be assessed a civil penalty up to $500 or other disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disqualification of agency personnel for bias and substitution
rubrics_metrics.description: Any individual serving alone or with others as an agency head may be disqualified from serving in an agency proceeding for bias, prejudice, or interest when any party shows just cause by a suggestion filed within a reasonable period prior to the proceeding. If the disqualified individual was appointed, the appointing power may appoint a substitute; if elected, the Governor may appoint a substitute. If a quorum remains after disqualification, a substitute may not be necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any action taken by a duly appointed substitute is as conclusive and effective as if taken by the agency as originally constituted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial review: filing, venue, scope, standards, and remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: A party adversely affected by final agency action is entitled to judicial review. Judicial review shall be sought in the appellate district where the agency maintains its headquarters or where a party resides (or as otherwise provided by law) by filing a notice of appeal or petition for review within 30 days after rendition of the order. Judicial review is confined to the record transmitted and any additions allowed by statute. The court may order agency action required by law, set aside agency action, remand for further proceedings, or provide other appropriate relief. The court shall not substitute its judgment for the agency’s on the weight of evidence for disputed facts but shall set aside or remand if findings are not supported by competent substantial evidence. The court may consolidate or transfer appeals and consider factors like judicial economy and avoidance of inconsistent results. Petitions challenging rules as invalid exercises of delegated legislative authority are limited in certain circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing the petition does not itself stay enforcement, but supersedeas is granted as a matter of right where agency action suspends or revokes a license under reasonable conditions unless supersedeas would pose probable danger to health/safety/welfare. The court’s decision may be mandatory, prohibitory, or declaratory and may order ancillary relief deemed necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards/circumstances for remand or setting aside agency action
rubrics_metrics.description: The court shall remand a case to the agency for further proceedings or set aside agency action when it finds: (a) no hearing prior to agency action and validity depends on disputed facts; (b) agency action depends on any finding of fact not supported by competent, substantial evidence in the record of a hearing under ss. 120.569 and 120.57; (c) fairness or correctness impaired by material error in procedure or failure to follow prescribed procedure; (d) agency erroneously interpreted a provision of law and a correct interpretation compels a particular action; or (e) agency’s exercise of discretion was outside the range delegated, inconsistent with agency rule, inconsistent with officially stated agency policy or prior practice (without explanation), or otherwise in violation of constitutional or statutory provision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court shall not substitute its judgment for agency discretion issues; remand/set-aside limited to enumerated grounds. Also the court may make interlocutory orders to preserve interests pending further proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement proceedings: standing, notice, remedies, and defenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Any agency may seek enforcement by filing a petition for enforcement in the circuit court where the subject matter is located. A petition for enforcement may be filed by any substantially interested resident, but no action may commence prior to 60 days after the petitioner has given notice of the violation to the head of the agency, the Attorney General, and any alleged violator. If an agency has filed and is diligently prosecuting a petition for enforcement, others may not commence. A petition by a nongovernmental person shall be in the name of the State of Florida on relation of the petitioner. Remedies include declaratory relief; temporary or permanent equitable relief; fines, forfeitures, penalties, or other statutory remedies; or, absent specific statutory authority, a fine not to exceed $1,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court may ascertain facts not in the record under s. 120.68(7)(a); may consolidate enforcement petitions and petitions for review; will punish contempt for willful failure to comply; respondents may assert defenses including invalidity of statute or inapplicability of administrative determination. For imminent and substantial threats, the agency may bring suit for immediate temporary relief without preclusive res judicata effect. Court may award costs, reasonable attorney fees, and expert witness fees when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of noncompliance as first enforcement response to minor violations
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the policy of the state that agencies shall issue a notice of noncompliance as their first response to a minor violation of a rule when it is reasonable to assume the violator was unaware of the rule or unclear how to comply. A notice of noncompliance may not be accompanied by a fine or disciplinary penalty; it must identify the specific rule being violated, provide information on how to comply, and specify a reasonable time to comply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must review all rules and designate those for which violation would be a minor violation; a minor violation is one that does not result in economic or physical harm or adversely affect public health/safety/welfare or create a significant threat of such harm. Agencies must publish lists of designated minor rules on their websites, ensure enforcement personnel know the designations, certify designations when filing rules, and follow statutory deadlines (with initial certification/publishing deadlines noted). Designation does not apply to certain agencies (e.g., Dept. of Corrections, educational units, law enforcement regulation, teachers) and is not subject to challenge under this chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: References to chapter 120 include subsequent amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless expressly provided otherwise, a reference in any section of the Florida Statutes to chapter 120 or to any section or portions thereof includes, and shall be understood as including, all subsequent amendments to chapter 120 or to the referenced section(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies legislative intent about cross-references to chapter 120 to capture later amendments unless expressly excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Saving clause for circuit court proceedings and declaratory judgments
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this chapter shall be construed to repeal any provision of the Florida Statutes which grants the right to a proceeding in the circuit court in lieu of an administrative hearing or to divest the circuit courts of jurisdiction to render declaratory judgments under the provisions of chapter 86.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves alternative circuit court remedies and declaratory judgment jurisdiction despite chapter 120 provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency regulatory plan and rulemaking deadlines, publication, and certification
rubrics_metrics.description: By October 1 each year each agency must prepare a regulatory plan listing laws enacted/amended in prior 12 months that create/modify agency duties, stating whether rulemaking is required and, if so, whether notice of rule development has been published and the expected date to publish notice of proposed rule. The plan must list other laws the agency expects to implement by rulemaking before the next July 1 and state intended purposes (simplify, clarify, increase efficiency, reduce costs, delete obsolete rules). The plan must include certification by the agency head and principal legal advisor verifying review and regular review of rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication requirements: publish regulatory plan on agency website with hyperlink on homepage; deliver certification to the committee; publish notice in Florida Administrative Register with hyperlink. Plans must be maintained on an active website for 10 years. Deadlines: by November 1 publish notice of rule development for laws identified as requiring rulemaking but for which no notice was previously reported; by April 1 publish notice of proposed rule for laws requiring rulemaking (with specific extension/extension-notice procedures allowing extension to October 1). Agencies must file certifications upon compliance, supplement plans within 30 days after a bill becomes law if it substantively modifies delegated duties, and publish supplements. Failure to comply requires delivery of written explanation within 15 days after written demand by the committee or chair. Educational units are exempt from this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of Administrative Hearings when division is a party — assignment restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding s. 120.57(1)(a), a hearing in which the division is a party may not be conducted by an administrative law judge assigned by the division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures that when the Division of Administrative Hearings itself is a party, it cannot assign one of its own ALJs to conduct the hearing, preventing internal assignment conflicts of interest.
